blocks.x: Security for the models themselves: prompt-injection defense with measured block rates, jailbreak suites running in CI so regressions cannot merge, corpus integrity monitoring against poisoning, and containment for agents with real tool access — the attack surfaces the classic frameworks never named.
AI security is a new surface on the same old adversary

AI systems add attack surfaces conventional security never met: the model can be talked into things, trained on things it should not know, and probed for what it remembers. AI security is the practice of bounding that — injection-resistant retrieval, output guards, abuse detection, and red-team evals that run in CI like any other test.

The scope covers the whole stack: prompt and response paths, retrieval integrity (can an attacker poison the corpus?), model and data exfiltration, agent-tool abuse, and the governance that says which model may touch which data class.
Below: the failure modes specific to model-backed systems, the reference architecture that defends them, and the console that measures the defenses honestly.
Four AI-specific failure modes classic frameworks never named
Each of these exploits the layer between the model and the estate — the countermeasures treat prompts, corpora and agent tools as attack surface with owners, tests and gates.

widgets.title: AI defense in depth — click nodes for the control contract

nodes.label: API perimeter
nodes.detail: Rate limits, entropy screens and parity-detection telemetry at the model API — extraction campaigns are visible as anomalous probing patterns.

nodes.label: Input screening
nodes.detail: Injection screens on user input and retrieved content; documents carry data, never instructions — quarantine enforced.

nodes.label: Tool scope enforcement
nodes.detail: Tool calls validated against per-agent scopes and egress allow-lists; unknown arguments rejected before execution.

nodes.label: Output screening
nodes.detail: Commitment rules, DLP on generated content, PII policy per region — every block logged with evidence.

nodes.label: Model registry
nodes.detail: Signed weights, SBOM per artifact, provenance chain per version — supply-chain compromise requires breaking attestation.

nodes.label: Training loop security
nodes.detail: Feedback provenance tracked, anomaly screening before dataset merge, memorization testing pre-promotion.

nodes.label: Red-team program
nodes.detail: Versioned attack suites per channel in CI plus monthly human campaigns — resistance scores trend on the console.

widgets.note: Click nodes to read the control contracts. The red-team lane tests every boundary continuously — resistance is a measured trend, not an assertion.
